title: Explicit homotopy tensor model and its invertible target comparison
statement: Use [new-integral-residue-ordinary-monoidal], [def-weil-pbc-residue-exchange-comparison-interface], [new-integral-residue-tensor-presentation], [new-integral-residue-derived-monoidal]. Let F:C→D be an exact additive functor between braided monoidal Grothendieck abelian categories with monoidal closed structures and functorial flat resolutions. For B∈C and P∈K(C), define the target comparison from LF(QP) tensor LF(B[0]) to Q(KF(B[0]) tensor KF(P)) by inverse braiding, the coefficient degree-zero comparison, both LF counits, and the tensor counit of Q. If KF(P) is K-flat, this comparison is invertible. For monoidal left adjoint F and a specified tensor-derived counit ε:QH→K(B tensor -)Q, also construct the model map LF(H(QP))→Q(KF(B[0]) tensor KF(P)) using LF(ε), its counit, the homotopy single-tensor comparison, and the ordinary tensor comparison. Specialize these explicit constructions to the integral residue coefficients and actual inverse image.

proof.text: Construct all maps from the displayed standard comparisons. Exactness makes both LF counits invertible; the degree-zero comparison and inverse braiding are isomorphisms. Since KF(P) is K-flat, the tensor counit of Q is invertible. Compose these isomorphisms. The concrete model map retains its original inline balanced tensor counit; its proved defining equation identifies this with the named residueExchangeTensorCounit.

Expose normalization of the canonical tensor presentation: expand derivedTensorPresentationIso and derivedTensorSingleIso, cancel inverse braiding and the coefficient comparison, then use leftDerivedNatTrans_app twice. Expose defining equations for the concrete model target and map.
Use the proved canonical counit and its presentation equation from IntegralResidueTensorCounit.
